# Feature Index Strategy

## The Two-File Pattern

To keep `.feature` files understandable beyond their file paths, maintain two separate files in the `features/` directory:

### 1. `features/README.md` — Human-Curated (You Own This)
A hand-written document explaining the project's BDD conventions, domain glossary, and any prose context a new developer needs. This file is never auto-generated or overwritten by scripts.

### 2. `features/INDEX.md` — Auto-Generated (The Script Owns This)
A Markdown table automatically generated by `bdd_utils.sh index`. It provides a machine-maintained, always-accurate mapping of every `.feature` file to its `Feature:` description.

Generate or update it by running:
```bash
./bdd_utils.sh index ./features ./features/INDEX.md
```

This separation ensures:
*   The index is **never out of sync** with the actual files on disk.
*   Human-curated context in `README.md` is **never wiped** by a script run.
*   CI/CD can regenerate `INDEX.md` on every commit as a verification step.

## What the Index Provides

The auto-generated table translates the shorthand `<aspect>` in a file path into the full capability description extracted from the `Feature:` line inside the file:

| Domain | Layer | Seq | Feature File | Capability Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **billing** | **api** | 10 | `billing/api/checkout-10.feature` | Checkout and payment processing |
| **billing** | **web** | 10 | `billing/web/cart_ui-10.feature` | Shopping cart user interface |

## Additional Columns (Manual)

If your project needs extra metadata columns (e.g., `Target Production File`, `Status`, `BDD Step Definitions`), maintain those in a separate hand-curated table in `features/README.md`. The auto-generated `INDEX.md` intentionally stays minimal so it can be regenerated cleanly at any time.
